content.title: What are Set and HashSet?
content.description: Set is an interface in the Java Collections Framework that stores unique elements without duplicates. HashSet is a hash table-based implementation of the Set interface that provides fast insertion, deletion, and lookup operations.

content.content: Unlike a List, which allows duplicate elements and maintains insertion order, a Set stores only unique values. HashSet is the most commonly used implementation because it offers excellent performance for storing and searching elements using hashing.

content.title: Why Use HashSet?
content.content: HashSet automatically prevents duplicate elements and provides nearly constant-time performance for most operations.
The Set interface represents a collection of unique elements. It does not allow duplicates and generally does not support index-based access.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Use Set whenever duplicate values should be eliminated automatically.

content.content: The HashSet class is available in the java.util package and is commonly used because of its fast performance.

content.title: Guest List
content.content: A HashSet is like the guest list for an event. Every guest's name can appear only once. If someone tries to register twice, the duplicate entry is ignored.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about Set vs List, HashSet internals, hashing, duplicate handling, equals() and hashCode(), and differences between HashSet, LinkedHashSet, and TreeSet.

items.question: Does HashSet preserve insertion order?
items.answer: No. Use LinkedHashSet if insertion order must be maintained.

items.question: Can HashSet contain duplicate elements?
items.answer: No. Duplicate elements are automatically ignored.

items.question: Can elements be accessed using indexes?
items.answer: No. HashSet does not support index-based access.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: HashSet stores only unique elements and provides fast insertion, deletion, and searching using hashing.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Use LinkedHashSet for insertion order and TreeSet for sorted data.
